Question: Does Arogya Supreme provide sum insured refill? | Answer: Yes, 100% refill of base sum insured once per policy year when sum insured is exhausted.
Question: Does Arogya Supreme offer E-Opinion? | Answer: Yes, insured can avail multiple e-opinions from empaneled medical practitioners during policy period.
Question: Does Arogya Supreme cover preventive health check-up? | Answer: Yes, preventive health check-ups are provided annually from the first renewal year.
Question: What is the cumulative bonus in Arogya Supreme? | Answer: 15% increase in sum insured each claim-free year, up to 100% of base sum insured.

Question: Who is eligible for the Divyanga Suraksha, SBI General Insurance policy? | Answer: All persons with disability who have at least one of the specified disabilities defined under The Rights Of Persons With Disabilities Act, 2016 with a valid disability certificate, as well as individuals with HIV/AIDS as per the Human Immunodeficiency Virus and Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017, are eligible to enroll in this product.

Question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases in Divyanga Suraksha policy? | Answer: Expenses related to pre-existing diseases and their direct complications are excluded until the expiry of 24 months for pre-existing disability and 36 months for all other pre-existing conditions (except HIV/AIDS), provided there is continuous coverage from the date of inception of the first policy with the insurer.

Question: What benefits are provided under inpatient care hospitalization cover? | Answer: The policy provides coverage for medical expenses incurred during hospitalization including room rent, boarding, nursing expenses (up to 1% of sum insured per day), ICU charges (up to 2% of sum insured per day), surgeon and medical practitioner fees, anesthesia, blood, operation theatre charges, medicines, diagnostics, and approved procedures.

Question: Does the policy cover expenses for AYUSH treatments? | Answer: Yes, the policy indemnifies medical expenses incurred for inpatient care treatment under Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy systems in an AYUSH hospital up to 50% of the sum insured per policy year.

Question: What are the sub-limits for room rent and ICU charges under this policy? | Answer: Room rent, boarding, and nursing expenses are covered up to a maximum of 1% of the sum insured per day. ICU/Intensive Cardiac Care Unit charges are covered up to a maximum of 2% of the sum insured per day.

Question: Is there a co-payment clause applicable? | Answer:  Yes. Each claim under the policy is subject to a 20% co-payment on the admissible claim amount, unless the waiver for co-payment is opted by paying additional premium.
Question: Are cataract treatments covered by this policy? | Answer: Yes, medical expenses for cataract treatment are covered up to INR 40,000 per eye, per policy year.

Question: What is the coverage for ambulance services? | Answer: Reasonable and customary expenses for emergency ground ambulance services are reimbursed up to INR 2,000 per hospitalization, subject to policy conditions.
Question: What is the age eligibility for children and adults under this insurance? | Answer: The policy is available for adults aged 18 to 65 years and children (newborn to 17 years).

Question: What waiting period applies for specific diseases and illnesses? | Answer: There is a 24-month waiting period for a list of specified diseases and surgical procedures unless arising due to an accident.

Question: What medical expenses are excluded from coverage? | Answer: Expenses related to diagnosis only, rest cure, rehabilitation, obesity surgery not meeting specified criteria, cosmetic or plastic surgery unless medically required, hazardous sports, breach of law, alcohol/drug abuse, non-prescribed supplements, unproven treatments, sterility, infertility treatments, and medical treatments received outside India are all excluded.

Question: What are the requirements for claim submission? | Answer: Claims must include a completed claim form, identity proof, original itemized bills, payment receipts, medical practitioner’s prescription for admission, discharge summary, investigation reports, OT notes for surgeries, implant invoices, and any other relevant documents specified by the company.

Question: How long is the grace period for renewal payments? | Answer: A fixed grace period of 30 days is allowed for yearly premium payment mode; for all other payment modes, a 15-day grace period is provided.

Question: Can the policy be renewed if there have been claims in previous years? | Answer: Yes, renewal shall not be denied on the grounds that the insured person has made claims in preceding policy years.

Question: What procedures are covered under modern treatment benefits? | Answer: The policy covers specific modern procedures such as uterine artery embolization, HIFU, balloon sinuplasty, deep brain stimulation, oral chemotherapy, monoclonal antibody immunotherapy, intra-vitreal injections, robotic surgeries, stereotactic radiosurgeries, IONM, stem cell therapy for hematologic conditions, bronchial thermoplasty, and more, up to 50% of the sum insured.

Question: How are maternity expenses handled under this policy? | Answer: Medical treatment expenses related to childbirth, complicated deliveries, caesarean sections (except ectopic pregnancy), miscarriage (unless due to accident), and lawful medical termination of pregnancy are not covered.

Question: What are the premium payment options and related conditions? | Answer: Premiums can be paid in lump sum, half-yearly, quarterly or monthly modes as per policy schedule. If installment is chosen, grace periods and coverage conditions apply as detailed in the policy.
Question: What happens if the sum insured is increased at renewal? | Answer: For any sum insured increase, the waiting period starts afresh only for the enhanced portion of the sum insured.

Question: What is the Free Look Period offered by the policy? | Answer: A free look period of 30 days from the date of receipt of the policy document is provided for new individual policyholders, allowing review and cancellation if dissatisfied.

Question: Who can be contacted for grievance redressal? | Answer: Complaints can be sent to the company’s customer care and escalated to the Grievance Redressal Officer; escalation procedures and contact details are specified in the policy documents.
Question: Who can purchase the Arogya Top Up Policy? | Answer: Any individual can purchase this policy for themselves and/or their family.
Question: What does the term "Family" mean in the context of this policy? | Answer: "Family" includes the self, spouse, dependent children, dependent parents, and parents-in-law.

Question: What are the minimum and maximum entry ages for the policy? | Answer: The minimum entry age is 3 months and the maximum is 65 years. The maximum entry age can be extended to 70 years if the insured opts for a deductible of ₹5,00,000 or more.
Question: Is there an exit age for the policy? | Answer: No, there is no exit age.

Question: What are the key benefits of the SBI General's Arogya Top Up Policy? | Answer: Key benefits include: no pre-policy medical test up to age 55, coverage of 60 days pre-hospitalization and 90 days post-hospitalization expenses, coverage for 141 day care expenses, and a wide coverage ranging from ₹1,00,000 to ₹50,00,000.
Question: What are the pre and post-hospitalization expense coverage periods? | Answer: The policy covers 60 days of pre-hospitalization expenses and 90 days of post-hospitalization expenses.

Question: What expenses are covered under eligible hospitalization? | Answer: Eligible hospitalization expenses include room rent, boarding, medical practitioners' fees (including teleconsultation), intensive care unit, nursing expenses, anesthesia, blood, oxygen, operation theatre expenses, surgical appliances, medicines and consumables, diagnostic expenses, x-ray, dialysis, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, cost of pacemaker, prosthesis/internal implants, and physiotherapy as inpatient care.
Question: Are maternity expenses covered? | Answer: Yes, maternity expenses are covered after the first 9 months.

Question: Are alternative treatments covered by the policy? | Answer: Yes, the insurer will reimburse expenses for alternative treatments like Ayurveda, Unani, Sidha, and Homeopathy if taken in a government-recognized institute.
Question: What are the ambulance expense limits? | Answer: The policy reimburses actual ambulance expenses or ₹5000, whichever is lower, per valid hospitalization claim.

Question: What is a "Day Care Treatment"? | Answer: A "Day Care Treatment" is a medical treatment and/or surgical procedure that is undertaken in a hospital or day care center in less than 24 hours due to technological advancements, but would have otherwise required hospitalization for more than 24 consecutive hours.

Question: What is "Domiciliary Hospitalization"? | Answer: "Domiciliary Hospitalization" is medical treatment for an illness or injury that would normally require hospital care, but is taken at home because the patient's condition prevents them from being moved to a hospital or because of a non-availability of a room in a hospital.

Question: Are expenses for mental illness covered? | Answer: Yes, expenses for inpatient treatment due to mental illness are covered up to the limit specified in the Policy Schedule, in accordance with the Mental Health Care Act, 2017. Certain disorders have a sub-limit of ₹1,00,000.

Question: What is a "Deductible" in the policy? | Answer: A deductible is a cost-sharing requirement where the insurer is not liable for a specified rupee amount, and this amount must be paid by the insured before the benefits are payable by the insurer. A deductible does not reduce the sum insured.

Question: What is a "Co-payment" in the policy? | Answer: A co-payment is a cost-sharing requirement where the policyholder will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claim amount. A co-payment does not reduce the sum insured.

Question: What is a "Pre-existing Disease"? | Answer: A pre-existing disease is any condition, ailment, injury, or disease that was diagnosed by a physician or for which medical advice or treatment was received within 36 months prior to the policy's commencement.

Question: What is not covered under the policy? | Answer: The policy does not cover treatment for intentional self-inflicted injuries or attempted suicide, or treatment related to disorders of intoxication, dependence, abuse, and withdrawal caused by drugs, alcohol, opioids, or nicotine.

Question: What is the purpose of the SBIG Health Super Top-Up policy? | Answer: The SBIG Health Super Top-Up policy provides financial protection against higher medical costs when your existing health insurance or base sum insured is exhausted.
Question: Who is eligible to be covered under the SBIG Health Super Top-Up policy? | Answer: Adults aged 18 years or older and dependent children aged 91 days to 25 years are eligible to be covered.

Question: What are the sum insured and deductible ranges for the SBIG Health Super Top-Up policy? | Answer: The policy offers a Sum Insured ranging from ₹5 Lacs to ₹4 Crores and a Deductible ranging from ₹2 Lacs to ₹2 Crores.
Question: Is there a maximum entry age for the SBIG Health Super Top-Up policy? | Answer: No, there is no maximum entry age for this policy.

Question: When will redemption fund payouts occur in April 2025? | Answer: They will take place depending on the TAT of the scheme (T1 to T10 days after transaction date).

Question: What clarification was issued for mutual fund transactions on April 1, 2025 (Annual Bank Closure Day)? | Answer: Subscription orders in liquid, debt, and equity schemes will be accepted. Liquid and debt orders will be forwarded to RTAs/AMCs on April 2, 2025. Equity orders will be processed for applicable NAV, but settlement may be impacted by banking system availability.

Question: How will redemption orders be processed on April 1, 2025? | Answer: Valid redemption orders for equity, liquid, and debt schemes will be reported to RTAs/AMCs on April 1, 2025. Redemption proceeds will follow the applicable TAT.
Question: What charges are levied on dormant mandates in BSE StAR MF platform? | Answer: NPCI levies annual maintenance charges on dormant mandates as per their circulars.

Question: What facility has BSE introduced to avoid dormant mandate charges? | Answer: BSE has activated Mandate Cancellation facility on StAR MF platform to allow cancellation of dormant mandates. From March 27, 2025, Exchange will initiate cancellations if members do not act.

Question: What changes are being introduced to nomination facilities in mutual funds? | Answer: From June 1, 2025, additional nominee details (Identity Number, Address, Email, Mobile) will be included in UCC structure, expanding to 183 fields. Revised NCT structure will allow nominee updates via bulk upload/API.

Question: What is the settlement programme for mutual funds in May 2025? | Answer: It includes subscription, liquid, and redemption transaction schedules from May 1 to May 31, 2025, with payouts based on scheme TATs (T1 to T10).
Question: When will redemption funds payout take place in May 2025? | Answer: Redemption payouts will occur depending on the scheme’s TAT, ranging from T+1 to T+10 days.

Question: What update was issued regarding nomination facility revamp on April 11, 2025? | Answer: The revised UCC structure for nominee details will continue to have 183 fields. It will be implemented across Manual, Bulk, Mobile, and API modes.

Question: What new facility has been added for cheque collection on BSE StAR MF? | Answer: HDFC Bank has been added as a new cheque collection agency for mutual fund purchase payments on the BSE StAR MF platform.

Question: Who can use the HDFC Bank cheque collection facility? | Answer: Clients of Mutual Fund Distributors (MFDs), Registered Investment Advisors (RIAs), and MFIs can use this facility to make payments towards purchase orders.

Question: What update was announced regarding Credit MIS reporting for mutual funds? | Answer: A new Credit MIS file format (Version 2.0) is being implemented for mutual fund transactions. Existing Version 1 and new Version 2 will run concurrently.

Question: What are common reasons for mismatch in funds mapping in MIS reporting? | Answer: Incorrect data in MIS, delayed uploads, incorrect client details (bank account/IFSC), mismatched amounts, incorrect UTR details, and delayed response from banks/NPCI.

Question: Which HSBC Mutual Fund schemes had their subscription suspension revoked? | Answer: HSBC Credit Risk Fund and HSBC Low Duration Fund subscriptions resumed from April 29, 2025.

Question: What facility was enabled on May 6, 2025, for nomination details in mutual funds? | Answer: Members can now update additional nominee details under existing UCCs through bulk upload or manual process.

Question: What new service area was added in the BSE CRS portal for mutual funds? | Answer: A new 'MF Settlement' tab has been added for settlement-related complaints like allotment, funds mapping, redemption, refund, and switch.

Question: What is the settlement programme for mutual funds in June 2025? | Answer: It includes subscription (liquid and non-liquid) and redemption transaction schedules from June 1 to June 30, 2025, with payouts based on scheme TATs (T1 to T10).

Question: What change was announced regarding redemption cut-off timings for overnight mutual fund schemes? | Answer: Effective June 1, 2025, redemption/switch cut-off timings for overnight schemes have been revised from 3:00 PM to 7:00 PM.

Question: What happens if nominee details are not updated in UCC for SIP orders from June 1, 2025? | Answer: SIP/X-SIP orders triggered on or after June 1, 2025, without updated nominee details may be rejected.

Question: What file must be updated to avoid rejection of SIP/X-SIP orders? | Answer: Members must update additional nominee details using the 56-field modification file before processing transactions.
